xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF ingested from GitHub issue #3505

plan.title: feat(verify): detect when lifecycle paths are hidden by any ignore mechanism

narratives.Description: Lifecycle gates only see tracked artifacts, so a hidden xbrief/active root in .git/info/exclude fails silently. Add verify:lifecycle-visible that reports ignore rules and skip-worktree flags on lifecycle roots, warn-first from session:start, without tripping deliberate selective entries.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Nothing detects when a clone's ignore configuration makes lifecycle artifacts untrackable. #3504 is a live instance: a bare `xbrief/active/` in `.git/info/exclude` silently hid every active brief on a maintainer machine, and it was found only by accident three weeks later.

Every lifecycle gate reads **tracked** artifacts. None checks whether the artifacts *can be* tracked.

## The gap

`verify:completed-tracked` (#3264 / #3476) asks "is this brief's land on the delivery tip?". `verify:orphan-active` (#2321) asks "is this active brief orphaned?". Both operate on artifacts git can see. When git is configured not to see them, both go quiet — the failure mode is silence, not an error.

Four mechanisms can hide a path, and only the first is visible in review:

| Mechanism | Committed? | Visible to teammates |
|---|---|---|
| `.gitignore` | yes | yes |
| `.git/info/exclude` | **no** | **no** |
| `core.excludesFile` (global) | no | no |
| `assume-unchanged` / `skip-worktree` | no | no |

The last three are per-clone. Behaviour diverges between maintainers running identical commands, which is the hardest class of drift to reason about.

## Proposed check

A verb — `verify:lifecycle-visible`, or folded into an existing lifecycle gate — asserting that the lifecycle roots are not ignored and not flag-suppressed:

1. `git check-ignore -v` against `xbrief/{proposed,pending,active,completed,cancelled}/` and the legacy `vbrief/` equivalents. This already covers `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`, **and** `core.excludesFile` in one call — cheap and decisive.
2. `git ls-files -v` filtered for lowercase status letters, catching `assume-unchanged` / `skip-worktree` on tracked lifecycle files.
3. Report the **matching rule and its source file** verbatim, as `check-ignore -v` does. "Something is hiding your briefs" is not actionable; `.git/info/exclude:33:xbrief/active/` is.

Selective per-file entries under a lifecycle root are legitimate and must not trip this — `.triage-cache/*.jsonl` and the #1144 hybrid entries are deliberate. The check is about **roots being hidden**, not about every path under them.

## Design questions

- **Where does it run?** Not on the pre-commit quality gate — that is the #1704 chokepoint and this is a per-clone environment property, not a per-commit one. `session:start` is the natural home: it already reports branch/policy/tool state and runs once per session, which is exactly the cadence for "your clone is configured wrongly."
- **Warn or fail?** Warn-first, as `verify:telemetry-coverage` shipped. A hidden lifecycle root is nearly always a mistake, but failing closed on day one would block maintainers with historical local excludes before they know why.
- **Is a hidden root ever legitimate?** If someone can name a real case, the check needs a documented opt-out; if not, it should eventually fail closed.

## Acceptance

- A bare `xbrief/active/` in `.git/info/exclude` is reported, naming file and line.
- The same via `.gitignore` and via `core.excludesFile` is reported.
- A `skip-worktree` flag on a tracked brief is reported.
- Deliberate selective entries (`.triage-cache/*.jsonl`, #1144 hybrid) do **not** trip it.
- The report names the rule, not just the symptom.

## Why it is worth building

The framework's entire lifecycle guarantee rests on artifacts being visible to git. That precondition is currently assumed and never verified, and #3504 shows it can be false for weeks without anyone noticing — on the framework's own repo, while shipping gates that depend on it.

Refs #3504, #3495, #3476, #3264, #2321, #1358, #1144
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer, I want session start to report hidden lifecycle roots, so that clone-local ignore drift cannot silently drop active briefs.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Implement verify:lifecycle-visible using git check-ignore -v on lifecycle roots and git ls-files -v for skip-worktree or assume-unchanged flags, naming the matching rule and source file.
2. Wire it warn-first into session:start, ignore selective entries such as .triage-cache jsonl, and cover exclude, gitignore, core.excludesFile, and skip-worktree fixtures.
